$comment: Where S11 and S12 may write, by (writer, override) pair. THE ROWS ARE DERIVED, not remembered: `destinations.closure()` reads every script package.json files[] ships plus the writers declared `writer_scope: author`, finds each environment read whose value reaches a write in that file, and `inventory_problems()` fails in both directions. The first version of this table was written from memory and was wrong both ways — it lacked nine overrides real writers read, and it certified AGENT_BIOS_STATE_DIR for install.sh, which assigns STATE_DIR from $HOME unconditionally (install.sh:48) and never reads that variable, so the certificate was about a value that cannot reach the writer. The class is a judgement over the derived pair: the override's own meaning decides it (config homes and state roots are install_roots, ZDOTDIR is launcher_shell_integration, the distill state is nudge, a HOME-derived personal layer is personal_layers), and a writer no §10.6 effect can invoke is named in not_a_destination with the reason it cannot. `derived_at_line` is the line the derivation found, for a reader; nothing reads it, and it is not authority.

writers.$comment: Compiles the instruction payload into the two config homes and the state root; the run hands it the environment it must write under.
The install canary writes its marker under the state root and the Claude config home to prove a deploy reached them.
Reads and rewrites the private installation's stored state under the state root and both config homes.
Writes the desktop app bridge's files under the owner's home.
Imports an instruction corpus into paths rooted at the owner's home.
The private installer: it writes the catalog, the store, the launcher status and the shell hook across the state root, both config homes and ZDOTDIR.
Writes the per-session instruction selection under the owner's home.
Provisions the managed venv and writes setup state under the owner's home.
Owns the instruction store under the state root.
Writes the understanding records into whichever host's config home the call names — the override key itself is chosen at runtime, so both keys are rows.
Prunes backups under the state root.
Writes the Windows shortcut and its state under the state root; on this platform no apply reaches it, but the pair is real and classified rather than excused.

The compatibility installer. It resolves both config homes and ZDOTDIR from the environment AND fixes STATE_DIR, BIN_DIR and LAUNCH_DIR from $HOME with no override at all (install.sh:48, :47, :45) — which is why an AGENT_BIOS_STATE_DIR row for this writer certified a value it cannot use.
The launcher: it writes its profile, venv, update-check and version state, the distill nudge state, and reads both config homes to place per-host files.

fixed_roots.root: local host="$1" foreign="$2" state="$HOME/.local/share/agent-bios" first prog stamp

writers.$comment: The shell function caches a host's subcommands under the state root.
Creates the managed venv at AGENT_LAUNCH_VENV.
Owns the shell connection: the .zshrc block under ZDOTDIR and the receipt and backups under the state root.

Reads the owner's home to take the census. Its only writes go inside the run directory; the HOME pair is a row because the derivation sees the read reach a write, and the class states what the run may not do with it.

The nudge state of §10.6, written by a script the owner runs from a checkout. It is NOT in package.json files[], so the derivation over the shipped set cannot see it; `writer_scope: author` declares that, and inventory_problems fails if files[] ever ships it or it disappears.
The Claude wrapper writes its session log under the Claude config home.
The Codex helm writes its state under the Codex home.
The Codex wrapper writes its session state under the Codex home.
The frame filter writes its cache under the state root.

One commit per applied item. The destination is the working tree the run was given, which has no environment override: the confinement is that the tree is the fixture clone named by the `checkout` class, never a worktree sharing the owner's .git.

The close writes the ledger, the version registry and the coverage state, all inside the checkout. The nudge is its own class because it is written last and by another writer. This file does not exist yet (S11/S12 are STAGE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED); the row is a forward declaration and INVENTORY_FORWARD_LANDED fails when the file appears, so the derived closure takes over rather than this row standing unchecked.

A personal-layer patch is applied under the owner's own layer root. HOME is required with no fallback declared, because a personal layer resolved from the password database is the one case where a missing override writes outside every root the run named. This file does not exist yet (S11/S12 are STAGE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED); the row is a forward declaration and INVENTORY_FORWARD_LANDED fails when the file appears, so the derived closure takes over rather than this row standing unchecked.

Recovery writes only its own journal and report, under the class whose root exists so that a recovery after a drifted apply has somewhere to land that the apply did not touch. This file does not exist yet (S11/S12 are STAGE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED); the row is a forward declaration and INVENTORY_FORWARD_LANDED fails when the file appears, so the derived closure takes over rather than this row standing unchecked.
The write-ahead journal itself. It is runtime state rather than part of the run so that a run directory lost with its machine does not take the record of what was already applied with it.

not_a_destination.reason: The uninstall archive is written only by `install.sh uninstall`, which no operation in §10.6's vocabulary invokes.
